note: Re-judged 2026-11-08 (independent auditor) after ed52d128eb strengthened TestClientLCPMagicNakRedrawsAndUsesNegotiatedValue. Section 6.4: "If the Magic-Number is equal to the one sent in the last Configure-Nak, the possibility of a looped-back link is increased, and a new Magic-Number MUST be chosen." The client unit reflects ze's own Configure-Nak (suggestion S for the server's zero Magic) back as a Nak of ze's request, which is exactly the looped case; it now requires the next Configure-Request's Magic to be nonzero, different from clientMagic and different from S, and the Echo-Reply to carry it. The prior finding (a client adopting S passed) is resolved: adopting S, keeping the old value or sending zero each fails it. Client producer read: negotiateLCP's Magic Nak branch calls generateDifferentMagic(localMagic), a fresh crypto/rand draw that is nonzero and not the previous value, and never adopts the suggestion. The verdict rests on the ppp pair, unchanged: TestRFC1661LoopedNakMagicChoosesNewMagic (+) and TestRFC1661LoopedNakMagicRefusesRepeatedDraw (-, forced repeated draw), plus TestMagicNumberRedrawnOnNak. Observation, not a finding: the client unit's two tags sit on the same assertions, and its draws are random, so dropping the magic != previous guard in generateDifferentMagic would survive it (only a 2^-32 draw shows it); the forced-repeat negative exists for the ppp role only.
